walkthroughs.body_html:
On the Wild Side — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

On the Wild Side brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with On the Wild Side.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Net primary productivity equals gross primary productivity minus:
options: energy lost in respiration by producers
energy gained from consumers
energy reflected by leaves
energy stored as starch

mcqs.q: Bare rock colonised first by lichens, then mosses, then larger plants is an example of:
options: succession
eutrophication
speciation
predation

mcqs.q: New species can form when populations become:
options: reproductively isolated
larger in number
more closely related
exposed to the same conditions

mcqs.q: Rising atmospheric CO2 increases warming because CO2:
options: absorbs and re-emits infrared (long-wave) radiation
reflects sunlight back to the surface
destroys the ozone layer
blocks all incoming sunlight

mcqs.q: Why is energy lost between trophic levels?
options: Energy is lost because predators eat only a few prey.
Energy is destroyed as it moves up a food chain.
Energy is lost mainly through respiration (as heat), movement and undigested or excreted material, so less passes on.
New species form whenever two different animals mate.
New species form whenever two different animals mate.
CO2 warms the Earth by reflecting extra sunlight onto the ground.
A new species forms the moment one individual gains a useful mutation.
Populations become reproductively isolated and accumulate genetic differences until they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

mcqs.q: Why does more atmospheric CO2 warm the Earth?
options: CO2 warms the Earth by making a hole in the ozone layer.
CO2 warms the Earth by reflecting extra sunlight onto the ground.
CO2 absorbs outgoing infrared (long-wave) radiation and re-emits some back toward the surface, trapping heat.
Energy is lost because predators eat only a few prey.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Net primary productivity”?
options: The directional change in a community over time, from a pioneer community through seral stages to a stable climax community.
The warming of Earth's surface caused by gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation.
The formation of new species when populations become reproductively isolated and diverge through natural selection or genetic drift.
The chemical energy stored by producers after subtracting energy lost in respiration; the energy available to the next trophic level.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Gross primary productivity”?
options: The warming of Earth's surface caused by gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation.
The formation of new species when populations become reproductively isolated and diverge through natural selection or genetic drift.
The total rate at which producers convert light energy into chemical energy in organic compounds by photosynthesis, per unit area per unit time.
The chemical energy stored by producers after subtracting energy lost in respiration; the energy available to the next trophic level.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Succession”?
options: The warming of Earth's surface caused by gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation.
The directional change in a community over time, from a pioneer community through seral stages to a stable climax community.
The total rate at which producers convert light energy into chemical energy in organic compounds by photosynthesis, per unit area per unit time.
All the living organisms (biotic factors) and non-living conditions (abiotic factors) interacting in an area, through which energy flows and nutrients cycle.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Greenhouse effect”?
options: All the living organisms (biotic factors) and non-living conditions (abiotic factors) interacting in an area, through which energy flows and nutrients cycle.
The chemical energy stored by producers after subtracting energy lost in respiration; the energy available to the next trophic level.
The directional change in a community over time, from a pioneer community through seral stages to a stable climax community.
The warming of Earth's surface caused by gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ecosystem”?
options: All the living organisms (biotic factors) and non-living conditions (abiotic factors) interacting in an area, through which energy flows and nutrients cycle.
The directional change in a community over time, from a pioneer community through seral stages to a stable climax community.
The chemical energy stored by producers after subtracting energy lost in respiration; the energy available to the next trophic level.
The warming of Earth's surface caused by gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Speciation”?
options: The formation of new species when populations become reproductively isolated and diverge through natural selection or genetic drift.
The chemical energy stored by producers after subtracting energy lost in respiration; the energy available to the next trophic level.
The directional change in a community over time, from a pioneer community through seral stages to a stable climax community.
The warming of Earth's surface caused by gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation.

sequence.def: Lifeless rock or sand with no soil
Lichens/mosses colonise and begin forming soil
Grasses and herbs grow as soil deepens
Larger plants outcompete and take over
